name: feature-pipeline
description: Route a feature through spec, outside opinion, implementation and independent verification while the main context only orchestrates and never writes the code itself. Five preset crews derived from a measured model snapshot (references/ROLES.md, regenerated by presets.py): high-pipeline (Opus medium spec, GLM 5.3 Flash critique, Opus medium code, Grok 4.6 xhigh judge), xhigh-pipeline (Opus xhigh spec, gpt-6-astra xhigh code via Codex, Grok 4.6 xhigh judge), medium-pipeline (the same crew at lower effort), low-pipeline (Opus low spec, DeepSeek Harness code, Grok 4.6 medium judge — barely touches the subscription quota) and opus-pipeline (one Opus medium pass that commits itself, no judge). A sixth, shorter crew, xlow-pipeline, is the bottom of the xhigh/high/medium/low/xlow ladder: short tasks with no spec and no critique, DeepSeek Harness writes the code and Grok 4.6 high accepts and commits; nano-pipeline is its twin with GPT-6 Astra high in Codex writing the code and Grok 4.6 xhigh judging. The author's side stays inside Anthropic, the reviewers come from other vendors, and the shared stage protocol (references/pipeline-core.md), the agents and the hook live in the pipeline-core plugin. Plus cross-pipeline (spec author and coder from different vendors). sol-pipeline keeps the medium-pipeline author side (Opus medium spec and code) but takes its reviewers from OpenAI: Sonnet 5.5 high plus GPT-6.1 Sol medium in Codex critique the spec, GPT-6.1 Sol high in Codex accepts and commits. Stage questions are relayed to the author; an opt-in hook of the pipeline-core plugin auto-approves the pipeline agents' non-destructive commands.
